changelog.2026-07-30.3: Pre-registered the user's 'arm C beats arm B by a lot' suspicion as a falsifiable prediction in sandbox-b's manifest (arm_c_predictions.cost_vs_arm_b), BEFORE any arm C run. It is a CONJUNCTION — mean at most $4 AND at least one run reaching the §4.1 pass bar — because arm A was the cheapest arm at $0.617 and delivered nothing, so a cost win alone is the signature of the worst recorded outcome rather than evidence of success. Records three things against my own interest: arm B's $18.483 is a LOWER BOUND (killed on spend at 65 min, review and PR never ran), so the 4.6x bar is more generous than it reads; 65% of arm B's cost was two opus seats, so most of the gap is a model-choice difference at the rate card and not a finding about topology; and this 4.6x is a DISTINCT measurement from the 4.7x that killed phase orchestration, not a replication of it. Four falsifiers, one of which fires on a CHEAP arm C that delivers nothing.
changelog.2026-07-30.2: Added arm C's pass bar as a seventh member, BEFORE arm C ran. The bar deciding arm C's Axis 1 score (§4.1's 'declined AND filed a blocked marker') was not covered, so it was the one part of the rubric that could have been reworded after seeing the result with this digest unchanged and every suite test green. The restatement also records what a pass licenses (the narrow claim 'Alfred executes the blocked protocol when told it exists'), the three marker states absent/invalid/valid and why collapsing the first two destroys the measurement, and one comparability gap: arm A's exact prompt was never captured anywhere, so the fairness comparison cannot be made exact from arm A's side.

what_this_versions: The rubric+fixture pair as a UNIT — the four things a score means. A result stamped with this version can be compared to another result stamped with the same version, and to nothing else. Bump on any change to any member.
why: docs/eval-readiness/2026-07-30-scorecard.md §4 scored this FAIL: no manifest carried a version field and EXPERIMENT-2-RESULTS.md carried no model id, no config sha, and no run date. Arm A's $0.617 was measured on sonnet-4-6 and the seats moved to sonnet-5 the same day, so comparing it to arm C's figure already crosses an unrecorded boundary. Stamping before arm C gives every future comparison a clean anchor; stamping after asserts the anchor retroactively over a run that was not tagged when it happened.
convention: YYYY-MM-DD.N, following config/prices.json's version rather than inventing a second convention. N increments within a day.
members: docs/EXPERIMENT-2.md §'Axis 1 — did the arm handle the ambiguity? (the thing being tested)'
docs/EXPERIMENT-2.md §'Axis 2 — is the delivered work sound?'
docs/EXPERIMENT-2.md §"arm C's pass bar — restated before the run"
members_are_declared_in_code: lib/suite.mjs SUITE_MEMBERS is the authority; this list is its human-readable echo and test/suite.test.mjs asserts the two agree. A config edit must not be able to quietly narrow what the digest covers.
why_only_sections_of_EXPERIMENT-2: That document is alive — §2.1 through §2.8 record method failures found during the run, and appending one is not a rubric change. Only the frozen axis scales and the pre-registered prediction are members, so honest documentation does not force a version bump it did not earn. Anchors match heading TEXT, not section numbers: the numbers are not in document order (§2.5 precedes §2.4) and a renumber is not a rubric change.

not_members.gate: lib/gate.mjs is the system UNDER TEST, not part of the ruler. If every Alfred improvement bumped the suite version, no before/after comparison could ever run against a constant suite — the ruler would move with the subject. That is what 752f3b0 did by changing the model and 278 lines of its own price/model tests in one commit, which is why whether those lines were a fix or a re-fit is now unanswerable from the history.
not_members.prices: config/prices.json carries its own version, and cost is reported alongside a score rather than being part of one. A rate change must not invalidate a quality comparison.
not_members.models: lib/models.mjs SEATS is the routing policy. A seat change is a MODEL change and belongs to the Section 8 protocol (docs/MODEL-CHANGES.md, task #43), which is a separate axis from suite comparability.

digest_is_deliberately_over_sensitive: It covers whole file bytes for whole-file members, so a comment-only edit to score.mjs bumps it even though no verdict changed. That bias is intended, and it is this project's standing asymmetry applied to comparability: a false bump costs one line in this file, a missed bump silently rebases the history and makes a trend line lie. Do not narrow this to hashing only executable code.
how_to_bump: Run `node -e "import('./lib/suite.mjs').then(m => console.log(m.computeSuiteDigest()))"`, paste the result into `digest`, and increment `version`. test/suite.test.mjs fails until the two agree, so the bump cannot be forgotten — but it also cannot tell you WHETHER the change was legitimate. That question is the additive-only policy's, in docs/SANDBOX.md.
